entries.text: I've got the p.c.r. Results on the two blood types from the gloves. Neither was Marty's. You were right, Mulder. She didn't do it.
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: I know that, you know that and so does whoever Marty's protecting, but Pennock is salivating right now. What we have to do is convince Marty. I got an idea. I'll get back to you.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: [ footsteps approaching ]
entries.speaker: Sound

entries.text: What do you want now?
entries.speaker: Marty Glenn

entries.text: I know who you're protecting, Marty, and I think I know why. You're protecting the man who murdered your mother.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: I don't know what you're talking about.
entries.speaker: Marty Glenn

entries.text: I read the original police report from 1970. Your mother died from a single stab wound to the right kidney, as did Paco Ordonez and susan forester. Dead at the hands of an unknown assailant.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: I never knew my mother.
entries.speaker: Marty Glenn

entries.text: No. I know. But for once you were there when it happened. She was pregnant with you at the time. She died on the operating table as doctors were trying to save her. You were born... Just barely. But the interruption of blood flow you suffered most likely caused your blindness.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: What does that have to do with anything?
entries.speaker: Marty Glenn

entries.text: I think that during that time... As you lost one sense... You gained another. And somehow... A connection was formed between you and your mother's killer.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: What connection?
entries.speaker: Marty Glenn

entries.text: You see through his eyes. You always have. You don't want to, you just do. And because of that you feel responsible for his actions, but you're not. And you're sitting here in prison... For crimes you didn't commit. It isn't going to accomplish anything, Marty.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: [ footsteps approaching ]
entries.speaker: Sound

entries.text: Excuse me, agent Mulder. She's being transferred now.
entries.speaker: Detective Pennock

entries.text: There's absolutely no point to you doing this. We're gonna find him with or without your help.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: I'm sorry.
entries.speaker: Marty Glenn

entries.text: [ buzzing ]
entries.speaker: Sound

entries.text: All right.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: [ chattering ]
entries.speaker: Sound

entries.text: Hi, Marty.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: What's going on?
entries.speaker: Marty Glenn

entries.text: Detective Pennock is with the warden right now arranging for your release.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: [ groans ] what?
entries.speaker: Marty Glenn

entries.text: Charges against you are being dropped. You're no longer a suspect in this case.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: How can they do that? I confessed.
entries.speaker: Marty Glenn

entries.text: A confession is worthless if it's a lie, and yours was a lie.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: [ sighs ] what have you been telling them?
entries.speaker: Marty Glenn

entries.text: Just that you're innocent, which is something they would've found out on their own anyway. The locker you sent us to? It had prints on it, but they weren't yours.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: I was careful.
entries.speaker: Marty Glenn

entries.text: Somebody else wasn't so careful. Charles wesley Gotts, an ex-con. Convicted in 1970 of aggravated assault. He was paroled three weeks ago, and he's been missing ever since.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: Never heard of him.
entries.speaker: Marty Glenn

entries.text: I happen to believe that, Marty. P.c.r. Test confirmed that it was his blood on the glove. The test confirmed something else, Marty. He's your father. That was the connection.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: Hmm.
entries.speaker: Marty Glenn

entries.text: Okay, we're all set. That is, if everything's taken care of on this end.
entries.speaker: Detective Pennock

entries.text: What's he talkin' about?
entries.speaker: Marty Glenn

entries.text: Detective Pennock has agreed to... Not pursue aiding and abetting charges if you agree to help us-- if you agree to help us find him. We need your help, Marty. You can end it now.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: I can end this.
entries.speaker: Marty Glenn

entries.text: I'm sure that's what you've always wanted.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: I never wanted to spend my life in a place like this. I had no choice. Hmm. If I help you, will you protect me until he's caught?
entries.speaker: Marty Glenn

entries.text: I will personally guarantee your safety.
entries.speaker: Detective Pennock

entries.text: Hmm. Take me home.
entries.speaker: Marty Glenn

entries.text: Moving into position at the back exit.
entries.speaker: Voice On Police Radio

entries.text: All right. Stand by.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: Copy that.
entries.speaker: Voice On Police Radio

entries.text: Just in time for the surprise party.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: She told you he'd be in there?
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: Yeah. She described this place perfectly, right down to the matchbooks.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: What made her decide to cooperate? She wants to stop him. All of a sudden? Why didn't she tell us his name before now?
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: She didn't know his name. They never met. He's been in prison her entire life.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: Yet according to you, she's been seeing through his eyes the whole time.
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: I don't think she was sure exactly what she was seeing. It was more like a constant image in her mind she learned to live with over time-- up until three weeks ago.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: When the murders started.
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: He was paroled and everything changed.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: Well, if all this is true, let's go get him. Mulder?
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: Everything's changed for her, Scully. I don't think we're gonna find him in there.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: Need some help over there? No. Shoulda known. Now, you know, you don't have to pack everything you own. I promise you, you're not gonna be in protective custody that long.
entries.speaker: Detective Pennock

entries.text: It's too late for that anyway.
entries.speaker: Marty Glenn

entries.text: Why's that?
entries.speaker: Detective Pennock

entries.text: Gotts is already here.
entries.speaker: Marty Glenn

entries.text: What are you talkin' about?
entries.speaker: Detective Pennock

entries.text: He's been keeping tabs on you for about a day. Now he knows where I live. He's reading the names on the mailboxes right now.
entries.speaker: Marty Glenn

entries.text: What? How could you--
entries.speaker: Detective Pennock

entries.text: [ grunts ]
entries.speaker: Sound

entries.text: How did you know he wouldn't be in there?
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: She misdirected us on purpose.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: She's still protecting him?
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: No, she's not. She never was. Pennock's not picking up.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: What do you mean?
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: It's not him she's been protecting. If he goes back to prison, so does she. Until now, she's never had a choice.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: [ clicks ]
entries.speaker: Sound

entries.text: [ whispers ] I hate the way you see me.
entries.speaker: Marty Glenn

entries.text: Mulder.
entries.speaker: Dana Scully

entries.text: She did this one. Trust me.
entries.speaker: Detective Pennock

entries.text: Not much to look at, is it? At least, that's what they tell me. You were at the sentencing, agent Mulder.
entries.speaker: Marty Glenn

entries.text: Is it my cologne?
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: No, I just knew you'd be there.
entries.speaker: Marty Glenn

entries.text: Marty, let me speak to the judge on your behalf.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: No.
entries.speaker: Marty Glenn

entries.text: We found where he'd been staying. It's a motel not far from where Paco Ordonez had been murdered.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: And before that, atlantic city. Hmm. I'd never seen the ocean before. And now, when I close my eyes, or even when I open them, that's all I see.
entries.speaker: Marty Glenn

entries.text: You're lucky he wasn't a fan of the ice capades.
entries.speaker: Fox Mulder

entries.text: [ chuckles ]
entries.speaker: Sound

entries.text: Lights out.
